body: From my experience with similar crashes in some games on my amd gpu and a long while of trying to fix it. The amd drivers aren't the most stable at the moment and stock settings can cause the gpu (at least in the case of a 9070xt) to sometimes boost up into unstable clock speeds. If the crash happens at a mostly random time that would be my guess for what the cause is.

Some updates:

- Another tester on RDNA1 architecture was able to replicate the behavior.
- I noticed that the scene in question was 998 kB, while similar scenes were only 30. It seems that some sort of scene inheritance error was causing the engine to balloon the `.tscn`'s filesize.
- Remaking the scene at 30 kB (while appearing identical) *seems* to have stopped the crashing for now, for both testers.

It looks like making a scene "incorrectly" under certain criteria causes some problem (with inflated filesize being a symptom) that triggers only on RDNA1 architecture. Whether or not other GPU architectures are able to just vault over the problem or if it was causing other underlying issues isn't known to me yet.

I've had two reports of users with RDNA1 GPUs (5600 + 5700 XT) having regular crashes in a game, on both the Vulkan and d3d12 backend. RDNA2 (and all other AMD + Nvidia hardware tested) has never had similar problems across a few hundred testers. I've been trying to collect more testers with this specific hardware setup to track down if its a fluke hardware coincidence, or Godot itself, but I just stumbled across this issue report which looks suspiciously remarkably similar to the problems I've been having

Boost clocks aren't the problem, as one tester specifically underclocked their GPU to rule that out, though it could be a faulty GPU. Its also not SDFGI, or SSIL that's been causing those testers problems either

I am also encountering this crash when playing around with shaders in the editor. It hasn't happened yet during play but my play sessions have been quite short.

same a the OP's tester it can happen randomly after a few minutes or not at all.

It happened with old drivers so I installed the more recent ones and go the same result.

Godot version: v4.7.2.stable.official
GPU: AMD Radeon RX 5700
Driver: Driver Version 25.10.45.05-260808a-203303C-AMD-Software-Adrenalin-Edition

Hi, I am also experiencing those kind of failures, my gpu is Radeon RX 5500 XT (8 GB), current godot version: v4.7.stable.official [5b4e0cb0f]

Following up with more data from my RX 5500 XT. I wrote a test harness that runs our full game world in fresh processes with D3D12 DRED forced on (auto-breadcrumbs and page-fault reporting, enabled from a small GDExtension before Godot creates its device), and it caught two hangs. Both DRED reports are attached.

**System:** Windows 11 Pro (build 26200), i7-13700K, Radeon RX 5500 XT 8 GB, driver 32.0.21045.5002 (2026-08-17), Godot v4.7.stable.official [5b4e0cb0f], Forward+, D3D12, 1920x1080 fullscreen, uncapped. Resizable BAR is off (256 MB BAR).

**Both hangs:**
- `DXGI_ERROR_DEVICE_HUNG`, device state HUNG, no page fault.
- The GPU hung about halfway through the opaque colour pass. The depth pre-pass and the shadow pass of the same frame had completed.
- For about 4 s before the reset, the core clock stayed pinned at ~1800 MHz while board power dropped to 3-4%. Temperatures were normal (66 °C at most). In the first hang the memory clock also dropped to idle (198 MHz).

| | Hang 1 | Hang 2 |
|---|---|---|
| Trees | GPU-culled (indirect MultiMesh, `ExecuteIndirect`) | GPU culling off (regular MultiMesh, no `ExecuteIndirect` in the frame) |
| Command list | 687 of 1373 ops completed | 563 of 1350 ops completed |
| First op not completed | `ExecuteIndirect`: draw 94 of 194 in the opaque pass | `DrawIndexedInstanced`: draw 76 of 152 in the opaque pass |
| Depth pre-pass / shadow pass | completed (194 / 198 draws) | completed (152 / 192 draws) |
| Afterwards | Driver never recovered: 286 TDR watchdog dumps, one per minute, until the PC went down | Recovered (one TDR) |

I inferred the pass boundaries from the clears and timestamp queries in the command list. Official builds don't name pipelines, so DRED can't say which material was drawing.

**Other observations:**
- Hang rate with the full world: D3D12, 3 hangs in about 2.8 h of test runs; Vulkan, none so far in about 1.8 h (not enough yet to call it a difference).
- A terrain-only version of the scene (Terrain3D with sun and environment, nothing else) ran 8.3 h without a hang. Another Godot 4.7 D3D12 project on the same PC has never hung.
- After the device is removed, the first error Godot logs is `buffer_create` failing with `0x887A0005`, as in #121402. That error is a consequence of the removal, not the cause.
- Possibly relevant, not verified: with Resizable BAR off, if I read the D3D12 driver right, `BUFFER_USAGE_DYNAMIC_PERSISTENT_BIT` buffers (#111183, new in 4.6) fall back to `D3D12_HEAP_TYPE_UPLOAD`, so per-draw instance data is read from system memory. #121402 also suspected persistent buffers and reports that 4.5.2 works.

I can run a test build through the same harness (for example with persistent buffers disabled, or with named pipelines so DRED can identify the material) if that would help.

_The test harness and this write-up were made with AI assistance. The numbers come straight from the attached reports._

[dred_hang1_executeindirect.txt](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/33036819/dred_hang1_executeindirect.txt)
[dred_hang2_drawindexedinstanced.txt](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/33036820/dred_hang2_drawindexedinstanced.txt)

Just as a follow up on my end in case it helps someone else: This issue appears to have gone away at some point in the production version of my game. The proximate change that caused the crash to go away was *substantially* lowering the rendered triangle count, by reducing the complexity of a single mesh (the terrain). This for the moment appears to have caused the crashes to mysteriously vanish for the 5xxx users, and there's been no further reports *yet*. If they do I'll try and grab some more interesting logs

Adding data from our shipped game (Tidy Up the Town, Godot v4.7.2.stable.official, Forward+). Three players have confirmed an **RX 5700 XT** with the same failure, on both D3D12 and Vulkan. Two more report the same symptoms (the whole PC locks up on launch and needs a forced restart) but haven't said which card they have.

| | Player A | Player B |
|---|---|---|
| OS | Windows build 26300 | Windows 10 19045 |
| CPU | Ryzen 5 5600 | Ryzen 7 5700X |
| Driver | 32.0.21045.5002 | 32.0.21030.2001 |
| Resolution | 2560x1440 | 1920x1080 |

The third player crashed on launch on both D3D12 and Vulkan; we have no log from them.

**What we see**

- At normal settings the device is lost on our main menu, usually 1 to 20 seconds after it appears, on both renderers and in both borderless and exclusive fullscreen. Some sessions lose it with no input or focus change at all.
- D3D12: the first error is already `0x887a0005` (DEVICE_REMOVED) from `buffer_create` / `texture_create`. One session started with `swap_chain_resize` returning `ERR_UNAVAILABLE`.
- Vulkan: `VK_EXT_device_fault` reports "No fault detected", then "Vulkan device was lost". One session's first error was `Couldn't get Vulkan surface capabilities (VkResult error -4)` in `swap_chain_resize`.
- Raising graphics settings mid-session on Vulkan gives a burst of `Couldn't create Vulkan graphics pipelines (VkResult error -4)` from `render_pipeline_create` (scene_shader_forward_clustered.cpp:506), then device lost. In other words, it dies during the pipeline recompile that a settings change triggers.
- One player's whole desktop corrupted ("all screens had mangled views") and needed a hard power-off, so this isn't only the Godot process.

**Agrees with 20k's finding:** dropping to the Low preset with **directional shadows off** gets all three players into the game and playing. Our main menu is the heaviest scene we have: about 2,200 MeshInstance3D, nearly all casting shadows, plus about 1,000 more meshes that a storm effect moves every frame, under a directional light with cascaded shadows. With shadows off, one player played for 28 minutes before a single device loss, which came at a focus-out (alt-tab) while a video may have been playing in another app.

**Not RDNA1-specific, possibly unrelated:** we also have device-lost reports from an RX 7900 XTX (Vulkan) and a GTX 1070 (D3D12), both in `WINDOW_MODE_FULLSCREEN` (borderless) and both right at a focus in or out. The 7900 XTX player also saw a 15 fps stutter only in borderless fullscreen while focused, gone in windowed and exclusive.

Our mitigation for now: we detect "Radeon RX 5700" in the adapter name and start those cards on Low with shadows off, cap the frame rate at 30 while unfocused, and after a device loss offer the other renderer or safe settings on the next launch. Full logs are available if useful. We can't run DRED on players' machines, but TudorDumitras's DRED reports showing `DEVICE_HUNG` mid opaque pass fit what we see.
